questions.prompt: Sam brings home $4,200 a month. Rent, food, transportation and other bills add up to $3,350. What is left each month before saving or extra spending?
Which of these expenses is most likely to change from month to month (a VARIABLE expense)?

options.text: A car loan payment set by your loan contract

questions.explanation: Dining out depends on your choices each month, so it varies. Loan payments, lease rent and flat-rate plans are set amounts — fixed expenses.

questions.prompt: A credit card has a $4,000 limit and an $800 balance. What is the credit utilization rate on this card?
Alex and Sam each owe $1,500 on cards with a 20% APR and make no new charges. Alex pays $200 every month; Sam pays only a $40 minimum every month. Which is true?

options.text: They pay the same total interest
Sam takes longer and pays more total interest
Alex pays more total interest because the payments are bigger

questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the remaining balance. Sam's smaller payment keeps the balance high for longer, so Sam pays interest for many more months and pays more in total.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the best fit for money in an emergency fund?

options.text: Concert tickets that are on sale
Your regular rent, which you already budget for
A sudden $900 car repair you need to get to work
A new phone because a new model came out

questions.explanation: Emergency savings are for unplanned costs that are not part of your routine monthly spending. Rent is routine, and sales or new models are wants, not emergencies.

questions.prompt: You put away $250 every month toward a $2,250 goal, starting from $0. How many months will it take?
A $2,000 credit card balance has an 18% APR. Using APR ÷ 12 as the monthly rate, about how much interest is added in one month with no payment?
questions.explanation: 18% ÷ 12 = 1.5% per month. 1.5% of $2,000 = $30. $360 is a full year of interest.

questions.prompt: You put $2,000 in an account earning 3% interest, compounded once a year. With no deposits or withdrawals, how much is there after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Year 1: $2,000 × 1.03 = $2,060. Year 2: $2,060 × 1.03 = $2,121.80. $2,120 is simple interest — it skips interest earned on interest.
